_doc: Everything about this paper that the page shows as data. mk_paper.py turns it into the headline card (parts/_gen_card.html), Further reading (parts/_gen_more.html) and the tables' data (parts/_gen_data.js). See html_utils/methods/papers.md.
title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
authors: Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Patrick Esser, Björn Ommer
lab: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and IWR, Heidelberg University; Runway ML

code.title: CompVis/latent-diffusion
code.note: the authors' PyTorch code and checkpoints, MIT licence (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path); Stable Diffusion's code is CompVis/stable-diffusion (about 15 minutes for the README), weights under the CreativeML OpenRAIL-M licence

run_label: generate with a toy latent diffusion model
takeaway: Runs DDPM in a mildly compressed autoencoder latent space with cross-attention conditioning, matching pixel-space quality at a fraction of the compute; became Stable Diffusion and made latent diffusion the default generative recipe.
verdict: Believe the idea and the efficiency: the compute ratios recompute from the paper's own tables, and every large image and video model since generates in a latent. Read the individual FIDs as single runs, several printed inconsistently between tables and figures, and "on par" in text-to-image as slightly behind GLIDE and Make-A-Scene.

headline.k: latent (f = 4) against pixel-space diffusion, same parameters
headline.d: train and sample throughput on inpainting, with 1.55 to 1.65× lower FID
against 4.59 for pixel-space ADM-G, with 3.5× less training compute (Table 18)

resources.n: the best visual walkthrough of the full pipeline (text encoder, UNet in latent space, VAE decoder); a good first read before the paper.
line-by-line PyTorch of the CompVis code, including the autoencoder, the cross-attention UNet and the samplers.
the practical component-level breakdown (VAE, UNet, scheduler, CLIP text encoder) with runnable code.
the modern retrospective on why two-stage latent generative models won, how autoencoder design trades reconstruction against modelability, and where the paradigm is heading.
an interactive walk through Stable Diffusion's denoising loop on real prompts, including the guidance scale; the full-size version of this page's toy.

kb.n: 2020-06: supplies the whole diffusion objective and the noise-predicting UNet; this paper changes only where the chain runs. Its page runs a toy DDPM and rebuilds the rate-distortion figure this paper's Figure 2 comes from.
2021-02: this paper trains its own BERT-tokenised text transformer; Stable Diffusion swapped in CLIP's frozen ViT-L/14 text encoder as τθ.
2020-10: DiT and its successors replace this paper's UNet with a Transformer on latent patches while keeping the latent space.
2017-06: cross-attention conditioning is the Transformer's encoder-decoder attention grafted into a UNet.
2021-06: the low-rank adapter that became the usual way hobbyists fine-tune Stable Diffusion's cross-attention layers.

topics.n: diffusion, VAEs and text-to-image in context.
